title: Quantum Memory in Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves
abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves are usually treated as a classical stochastic background sourced by phase-random curvature perturbations. We show that this description can miss residual quantum information. Starting from a decohered two-mode Gaussian scalar state, we derive explicit transfer relations between the scalar anomalous coherence and the covariance matrix of induced tensor modes. For a localized scalar power spectrum, the ordinary tensor power is sourced by scalar power contractions, whereas the opposite-mode tensor coherence is sourced by scalar anomalous-coherence contractions. This coherence can generate nonzero tensor discord and a connected tensor-power covariance even after scalar entanglement has vanished. We identify the connected covariance and phase-sensitive strain correlations as probes of primordial quantum coherence in secondary gravitational-wave backgrounds, and discuss their possible relevance for future space-based interferometers and pulsar timing arrays.
summary: This paper investigates the fate of primordial quantum information encoded in scalar perturbations as they generate gravitational waves. By analyzing decohered Gaussian states, the authors show that residual scalar coherence survives and manifests as measurable non-classical correlations—like tensor discord and connected covariance—in the induced gravitational wave background. These unique phase-sensitive signatures offer new targets for future space-based GW observatories.
main_problem: To determine if residual quantum information from primordial scalar perturbations can survive decoherence and manifest as detectable signatures in secondary gravitational-wave backgrounds.
main_result: Residual scalar anomalous coherence can generate nonzero tensor discord, connected covariance, and phase-sensitive strain correlations even after the initial scalar entanglement has vanished.
method: The authors derive explicit transfer relations linking the scalar anomalous coherence to the induced tensor covariance matrix using a Gaussian state description.
model_or_system: The study models Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves (SIGWs) generated at second order from decohered two-mode Gaussian scalar states, analyzing how quantum correlations propagate through nonlinear gravitational interactions.
key_observables: Gaussian tensor discord ($D_h(k)$), connected covariance ($\kappa(k)$), and phase-sensitive strain correlators ($\Gamma(k, q)$).
important_parameters: Decoherence strength ($\epsilon_{	ext{dec}}$) and the frequency/wavenumber spectrum of the source.
main_assumptions: The analysis works to leading non-trivial order in scalar perturbations and provides an order-of-magnitude scaling estimate for detectability, not a full sensitivity curve.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares various coherence measures (negativity, discord) showing persistence in the separable regime. Figure 2 illustrates the derived SIGW spectrum ($d_k$) and the connected covariance statistic ($\kappa(f)$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of quantum information loss during decoherence, derives transfer relations between scalar coherence and tensor observables, calculates specific diagnostics like discord and connected covariance, and discusses their potential detection using future interferometers.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete theoretical framework for how non-local quantum correlations (coherence) can be imprinted onto classical background signals (GWs), offering new diagnostic tools beyond simple power spectrum measurements.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Minimal scalar-to-tensor transfer benchmark. Panel (left) shows the scalar logarithmic negativity, Gaussian dis- cord, and anomalous coherence fraction as functions of the decoherence strength. The vertical line marks the point where scalar entanglement vanishes. Panel (right) shows the induced tensor coherence, tensor discord, and connected covariance generated by the same residual scalar anomalous coherence. The tensor quantities remain nonzero inside the scalar separa- ble regime because they are sourced by coherence contractions rather than by scalar entanglement itself.

FIG. 2. Kernel-derived benchmark signals from a lo- calized scalar source. Panel (a) shows the scalar-induced gravitational-wave spectrum obtained from the radiation-era transfer kernel for a log-normal scalar power spectrum. The vertical line denotes the scalar peak scale f∗. Panel (b) shows the connected covariance statistic κ(f) generated by the transferred tensor coherence for representative decoher- ence strengths. Both panels are computed from the same scalar spectrum and transfer kernel; the overall normalization is chosen for a representative detectable SIGW amplitude.
